title: Generic type arguments are not encoded properly

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: A fault in an existing feature

body:
XUnit encodes all of information about a test in a base64 value. This encoding, however, does not work for a test receiving types of generic arguments as its arguments. To demonstrate the issue we need R# Test Runner as it allows running a single test-case from all test-cases for a given theory. Steps to reproduce: 1. Create a unit-test project targeting latest .netcoreapp supported by xunit. 2. Create the following test class: ``` using System; using System.Collections.Generic; using System.Runtime.Serialization; using Xunit; namespace Repro { public class UnitTest1 { [Theory] [MemberData(nameof(Data))] public void TestReceivingGenericArgumentsAsParameters(Type[] args) { Assert.All(args, arg => Assert.DoesNotContain( arg.GetGenericParameterConstraints(), c => c == typeof(ISerializable) )); } public static IEnumerable Data() { var type = typeof(Component); var generic = type.GetMethod("Generic"); var constrained = type.GetMethod("ConstrainedGeneric"); yield return new object[] { generic.GetGenericArguments() }; yield return new object[] { constrained.GetGenericArguments() }; } } public class Component { public void Generic() { } public void ConstrainedGeneric() where U : ISerializable { } } } ``` 3. Build the projects and all test-cases of `TestReceivingGenericArgumentsAsParameters2` should be discovered by ReSharper. 4. Try running any one of them. 5. The test-case will become inconclusive and the following warning will appear in execution log: ``` [xUnit.net 00:00:00.34] XUnitTestProject2: Catastrophic error during deserialization:
